question: Evaluate $\int \frac{dx}{\sin(x-a)\sin(x-b)}$.
explanation:
Use the identity $\frac{1}{\sin(x-a)\sin(x-b)}=\frac{1}{\sin(b-a)}[\cot(x-a)-\cot(x-b)]$.

Thus the integral becomes $\frac{1}{\sin(b-a)}\int[\cot(x-a)-\cot(x-b)]dx$.

$=\frac{1}{\sin(b-a)}[\ln|\sin(x-a)|-\ln|\sin(x-b)|]+C$.

$=\frac{1}{\sin(b-a)}\ln\left|\frac{\sin(x-a)}{\sin(x-b)}\right|+C$.
